long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Porjus, Carl-Henric Svanberg studied engineering physics at Linköping University and business administration at Uppsala University. He began at ASEA, moved through Securitas, and became chief executive of Assa Abloy in 1994. There he helped turn a young lock group into a global security-products business through operating growth and more than one hundred acquisitions.

He became Ericsson's president and chief executive after the telecom crash and restored the network-equipment company to strength. Svanberg later chaired BP for eight years and Volvo Group for twelve, adding energy and transport governance to his industrial record. He subsequently led Sweden's AI Commission, whose roadmap proposed measures for national competitiveness, public administration and responsible technology use.
